summary: A first-person narrator, Marcus, recounts an intimate moment with a girl in a bedroom, which is interrupted when he realizes a press conference is about to start. The passage mixes the romantic and physical tension with his excitement over a social movement that is spreading around the city. It ends with the pair dressing quickly and heading to Patcheye Pete's, where the online game Clockwork Plunder is played by press members and by the 'Xnetters'.
one_line: Marcus recounts an interrupted intimate moment before a press conference, then heads to Patcheye Pete's to meet the press and Xnetters in Clockwork Plunder.
key_facts: The narrator, Marcus, says he had known since the night in the park that the girl would push things further physically.
Marcus describes the impending press conference, fights with his parents, international attention, and a movement careening around the city like a wild pinball.
Marcus says he was falling in love with the girl, whom he describes as beautiful, smart, clever and funny.
The two undress on the bed, and Marcus notes that only his socks remain on until he peels them off with his toes.
The bedside clock, which had rolled onto the floor, glows up at them and reveals the time.
Marcus yelps "Crap!" and says "It starts in two minutes!" as the reason they stop.
Marcus says that if asked beforehand he would have answered a resounding and unequivocal NO to stopping for a nuclear bomb, yet they stopped for this.
The couple dress hastily, grab their keyboards and mice, and head for Patcheye Pete's.
Press members are identifiable as noobs who play their characters like staggering drunks and offer strangers inventory or accidental hugs and kicks.
The Xnetters are identifiable by their tricked-out characters with cool weapons and booby-traps on the keys sticking out of their backs.
The Xnetters play Clockwork Plunder whenever they have spare time or do not feel like doing homework.
A passing line mentions an engineer living in Borujerd named Calvin.
